choices.title: Assumption

  • Hypothesis is stated in experimental studies. It is of two types: null and directional/non-directional hypothesis. The null hypothesis expresses the absence of relationship between independent and dependent variable. For example, there would be no decrease in pain perception among the neuropathy patients on administration of aroma therapy.
  • Directional hypothesis expresses the direction of relationship between independent and dependent variable as there would be a significant decrease in pain perception among the patients suffering from neuropathy after administration of aromatherapy with a significant p-value.
  • Non-directional hypothesis expresses the effect of independent variable on dependent variable, but the direction would not be there. Example: There would be a significant effect in pain perception among the patients suffering from neuropathy after administration of aromatherapy with a significant p-value.
  • Analytic method is the statistical test applied in order to interpret the data. It includes parametric and nonparametric tests.
  • Determinants are a factor that decisively affects the nature or outcome of something.

choices.title: Hypothesis
choices.correct_explanation:
• Statements formulated to predict a relationship between two or more variables is known as hypothesis.
  • Hypothesis is stated in experimental studies. It is of two types: null and directional/non-directional hypothesis. The null hypothesis expresses the absence of relationship between independent and dependent variable. Example: There would be no decrease in pain perception among the neuropathy patients on administration of aroma therapy.
  • Directional hypothesis expresses the direction of relationship between independent and dependent variable as there would be a significant decrease in pain perception among the patients suffering from neuropathy after administration of aromatherapy with a significant p-value.
  • Non-directional hypothesis expresses the effect of independent variable on dependent variable, but the direction would not be there. Example, There would be a significant effect in pain perception among the patients suffering from neuropathy after administration of aromatherapy with a significant p value.
  • Interpretation is stating the statistical analysis of data in terms of study objectives. Example: 58% of the women of age 18 years or above are having hemoglobin value of less than 19 mg/dL in a specified period and specific area or district.
  • Assumption is the universal truth that is necessary to state before starting the study. Assumptions the facts or beliefs necessary for completion of study. Example: Patients will provide the truthful information.
  • Analytic method is the statistical test applied in order to interpret the data; it includes parametric and nonparametric tests.

  • Lack of Oxygen saturation in arterial blood is termed as anoxemia. This condition can be manifestation of cardiopulmonary disorders.
  • Asphyxia: Lack of Oxygen and blood flow to the brain. Common condition is birth asphyxia observed in neonates.
  • Cyanosis is bluish discoloration of extremities (acrocyanosis) and mucous membranes (central cyanosis) usually observed when hemoglobin is less than 5 mg/dL.
  • Anoxia is a generalized condition of absence of oxygenation.

choices.title: Development of carcinoma
choices.correct_explanation:
• Commonest complication of hydatidiform mole is choriocarcinoma development. Hydatidiform mole can lead to choriocarcinoma of the uterus that is characterized by snowstorm appearance on imaging. Hydatidiform mole is characterized by raised level of beta human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG).
  • Sepsis is symptomatic bacteremia with or without organ dysfunction. It can lead to abscess and septic shock. Sepsis is observed in hydatidiform mole if infection prevention measures are not followed well.
  • Incomplete evacuation: This is a complication if mole is not removed completely, this can occur if size of mole is discrete or removal is done in absence of proper imaging showing extent of invasion into nearby organs.
  • Perforation: Less common complication. Usually seen in large size of moles that leads to perforation of uterus and other surrounding organs.

questions.title: Commonest complication of hydatidiform mole is:

choices.title: Bordetella pertussis
choices.correct_explanation:
• Bordetella pertussis is the causative organism of whooping cough. Pertussis is also known as whooping cough.
  • Whooping cough is a respiratory tract infection characterized by a paroxysmal cough.
  • Streptococci cause pneumonia, skin and skin structure infection, surgical site infections and gastrointestinal infections.
  • Corynebacterium diphtheriae is gram positive bacteria that cause upper respiratory tract or cutaneous infection. Schick test is done for its diagnosis.
  • Pneumococci are a gram positive catalase negative organism. It causes community- acquired pneumonia, bacterial meningitis, bacteremia, otitis media, sinusitis, septic arthritis, osteomyelitis, peritonitis and endocarditis.

choices.title: Bedside clinic
choices.correct_explanation:
• Bedside clinic is a method of teaching, which always entails the presence of the patient.
  • Bedside clinic is a process in which a clinical teacher and a group of learners sees a patient, elicits or verifies physical signs, discusses provisional diagnosis, diagnostic or therapeutic options in the clinical setting.
  • Nursing rounds is a clinical teaching method, according to Garber, it is defined as overview of certain aspects of nursing care if all patients in the ward or selected patients. In condition of time shortage, these rounds can be conducted at common counter and problems are discussed.
  • Group discussion is a teaching learning method where group is given a topic or problem and they are allowed to present their ideas among each other; positive criticism and critical analysis are important aspects of it.
  • Computerized study has no relevance here.

choices.title: Second lumbar vertebra and third lumbar vertebra
First lumbar vertebra and second lumbar vertebra
Third lumbar vertebra and fourth lumbar vertebra
choices.correct_explanation:
• Third lumbar vertebra and fourth lumbar vertebra is the site for lumbar puncture in adults as spinal cord ends at the level of L1 and L2. So, it is a safe practice to insert the spinal needle between L3 and L4. If a higher puncture is done, spinal cord injury may occur.
  • Lumbar puncture procedure is a diagnostic procedure where cerebrospinal fluid is aspirated for microscopic or metabolic indicators as well as to measure CSF pressure.
